$COHR earnings transcript TLDR:

Q: On $LITE + $MRVL merger.

A. Customers will prefer an independent optical supplier without competitive conflicts (opportunity for other merchant laser suppliers)

Q: Loop Capital asked about 2028 laser industry oversupply.

A: No oversupply risk by 2028. Coherent’s entire current internal InP production is consumed by its own products while its expanding capacity.

Q: On Chinese laser competition for CPO UHP lasers

A: “We really only have one competitor” (hinting at $LITE). 

Q: On financing concerns for capacity expansion during this market scare

A: Customer LTAs have prepayments, which are used for product capacity orders

2027 completely sold out, LTAs extend to 2030, customers placing orders into 2028.

Q: On laser technology for CPO scale up from Bernstein, whether it’s VCSELs or CW lasers.

A: CW for CPO scale out and scale up for 2026-2027.

2029-2030 sees scale in and chip to chip using micro-VCSELs, and 2028 opportunities for NPO scale up.

So technology of choice is CW for CPO.

- Coherent is seeing pricing power and raising margin targets, supporting view optical players get additional leverage for margin expansion

- Massive new $20B 5Y LTA, anchored by UHP CW lasers, with other optical products mixed in

- demand comes from growth in DC and conversion of copper interconnects to optics. The latter is bandwidth requirements, independent of DC growth.

slower compute growth can coexist with sharply rising optical content per system

TLDR:

- nothing quite showing optical demand like $20B in LTAs anchored by high power lasers from 1 customer alone (not your frontier labs type commitments)

- no industry wide laser oversupply risk by 2028 for InP lasers/EML 

- financing funded by revenue from LTAs and purchase orders.

- doesn’t see Chinese competition for high end lasers, commentary casts doubts over China capability + capacity expansion claims

- CW lasers weapon of choice for CPO, blended margins going up for optical players

- optics more isolated in the event of a DC slowdown 

Quite wild to see fundamentals of optical players improve so much, while overall valuations crash.

Holy sh*t. Claude Code just found a hidden chip inside my Chinese power bank from Guangzhou. Every time I charged my iPhone, it quietly copied the whole phone…

It also read our saved Wi-Fi password off my iPhone, got onto our home network and sent everything to a server.

I bought it for $19 at an airport kiosk there 3 weeks ago. No brand, 30,000 mAh on the label, and it felt heavy.

The first time I plugged in, the screen asked "Trust This Computer?". I tapped Trust without thinking and went on with my day. That one tap gave it access to everything.

This morning I finally set up Claude Code to warn me when any device starts reading my files. An hour later, 10 seconds into charging, the screen filled with yellow warnings, then red ones: data was moving when it should only be charging.

I asked Claude Code what was going on. My phone saw the power bank as a small computer with 64 GB of storage and its own internet connection.

A USB cable has wires for power and wires for data, and a normal charger only uses the power ones. This one used both, and it had already copied all of this:

→ /device → IMEI and serial number
→ /contacts → 1,206 numbers
→ /apps → every app I have, including my 2 bank apps
→ /photos → 3,912 pictures, my passport among them
→ /wifi → our network name and its key
→ /wife's iPhone → her photos too, she charged from it twice and tapped Trust too

Each time we plugged in, it used that key to get online and send out the new files:

sends to → 47.***.***.12

posts.text:
I can only reply to a minority of comments, and it’s usually luck-of-the-draw what I see when I’m online. And Twitter isn’t really the best place for long-form debates.

“Why do you think the legal system couldn’t prevent the Biden Admin from allowing millions of unknown foreign men to illegally enter the country?”

-Surely you’re aware of the asymmetry that courts are more able to block specific illegal actions than force officials to take positive actions that require funding. In other words, with a stroke of a pen a court can say,“no, those tariffs are illegal actually, you can’t use emergency powers for indefinite and broad new taxes” but it’s much harder to say, “you have to allocate more resources to the border.” To fix the latter you generally need an executive and legislative branch with the will to do it, which is partially what the 2024 election was a mandate on.

“Why can’t the legal system prevent criminals who’ve been arrested 37 times from being let back into society?”

-Places where people are arrested 37 times tend to be cities where the politicians and courts are in agreement. That’s the set of policies they have on the books and how the rules are being interpreted. If people get fed up with it they can elect people that will write and interpret stricter laws and sentences about repeated crime.

“Why couldn’t the legal system prevent billions of dollars of egregious welfare fraud?”

-Tons of cases are prosecuted each year. Even so, outright fraud is a small share of the spending. The bigger issue is healthcare bloat and demographics.

“Why can’t the legal system enact voter ID which is the most obvious and basic tenet of election security?”

-It’s not the role of the legal system to enact voter ID or other details around voting. That’s primarily within the legislative branch (unless the legislative branch does something that violates the Constitution).

“If you are so willing to label Trump a "fascist", perhaps you could assign a label to the people who fail to deliver the most basic functions of government? What label should they be given?”

-By definition, that description would be closer to anarchist.

Quick mini thread on tail risk hedging thanks to my man, @Fink_Money 

Tail hedging is a pretty complex topic and there are 10 more reasons why it can be challenging for a smaller investor to implement. But two of the biggest limitations from an infrastructure perspective is understanding what exactly to buy and how much to pay. Trying to execute on those two simple concepts have further nodes that have its own challenges. 

Ultimately, you’re trying to answer two questions. Which tails do you want to own, and at what price does owning them make economic sense?

A static hedge can struggle even if you’re right about the crash. Say you only buy one-month, deep OTM puts, and the market takes six months to grind lower, with sharp rallies along the way. You can be right about where spot ends up and still watch one set of puts after another expire worthless. That’s why I don’t put much faith in one-trick-pony hedges. You need infra to guide you on a core understanding of which tenors and strikes are likely to reprice based on positioning and how well those options carry as spot moves along the skew curve. 

Execution matters just as much. Say a tail option is quoted $0.02 bid at $0.10. It’s easy to look at the offer and think, “It’s a dime. How expensive can it be?” Suppose you pay $0.10, spot sells off, vol rises, and the option reprices to $1.00. Your position is worth 10× what you paid, a 900% gain. If you can work the order at $0.05, that same move takes you to 20× what you paid, a 1,900% gain. Getting filled at a nickel lets you own twice as many contracts. That’s where you double your convexity. You own twice the exposure going into the crash because of the infra you have to post liquidity and find a real inside market before spot or vol moved at all.

That’s the part I think is hard for a retail investor or a smaller shop to replicate. Even if you identify the right tails, you still need the infrastructure and execution logic to work orders at scale across names, tenors, and deltas, all at prices that make the hedge worth owning.
 
Start adding in how to offset the bleed in a real uncorrelated fashion along with a real alpha focused monetization framework and you have tons of other considerations to make when executing something like this.

quoted.text: I see lots of people on here looking for the secret sauce of fat tail hedging. To me it seems that you're never going to get FOTM options via retail platforms that are cheap enough to make it worth your while. You need to use a fund that buys them direct for peanuts.
